title: Paper Lantern Insights onramp ramble
content:
Context: quick scratch from sync 2025-02-15 with Paper Lantern Insights (PLI). They are evaluating a hybrid on-prem + VPC Private deployment to serve a customer-facing analytics assistant. Notes are messy — save for handoff to SE/AE.

Attendees:
- Jin Park (PLI, CTO)
- Sara Patel (PLI, Eng Lead)
- Maya Chen (Redwood SE)
- Ethan Brooks (Redwood Solutions)
- informal: product questions dropped in Slack #pli-onramp

High-level ask from PLI:
- Low-latency document Q&A for ~10k monthly active users; peak concurrency estimate 75-150 qps during reports windows.
- Data privacy: customer docs must never leave VPC; on-prem storage for PII.
- Embeddings-based retrieval + reranking for long documents (avg doc size 12k tokens).
- Budget target: keep per-query cost under $0.10 at 95th pct for typical Q&A flows.

Quick technical constraints (PLI):
- Kubernetes on-prem cluster (4x A100-ish), strict egress controls (only to Redwood control plane endpoint when permitted).
- They plan to host the vector DB themselves (Milvus).
- Session stickiness preferred for conversational flows; they want user-level context pinned for 5 minutes.
- Compliance window: must sign an NDA + SOC2 addendum before we ship a Private build.

Key gotchas / red flags from the call (brain dump):
1) Tokenization drift between retriever and model: their Milvus corpora use whitespace-tokenized text (legacy) — we need to ensure embedding model and tokenizer are aligned. Recommend: re-index with tokenizer-matched chunks (we suggested protobuf export + small re-chunk script).
2) Long-document preprocessing: their current chunk size is ~4k words -> unacceptably large for embeddings. Suggest 512-1024 token chunks with overlap 128.
3) KV cache management on Private: they will re-use sessions across users; we flagged potential memory blowup if we keep long KV caches for many sessions. Proposed policy: LRU per-user with 5-minute TTL and hard cap ~1.5GB per worker.
4) Autoscaling expectations: on-prem has limited burst headroom. Must plan canary + fixed burst policy. Redwood dedicated autoscaler strategies not fully available on-prem — note for engineering escalation.
5) Network egress: PLI's security requires intermittent approval windows for control-plane sync; need offline onboarding flow and signed attestations for model bundles so we can run without constant control-plane access.

Immediate recommended config (prototype):
- Model: open LLM aarch64-optimized 13B quantized (they want open weights). Start with v1.2 candidate (sits in our model catalog).
- Embedding model: small dense embedder (8k dims not necessary) — recommend 1536-d open embedder (cost/latency sweet spot).
- Chunking: 800 token chunks, 128 token overlap; store chunk metadata (doc_id, offset, original char span).
- Retrieval: FAISS-like index (they use Milvus) with cosine sim + async re-ranker pass using a narrow context window (1024 tokens) to rerank top 20.
- Serving: 2x workers per A100 node, pinned to GPU, memory reserve 20% for cache.
- Caching: prefix caching for repeated report prompts + top-20 rerank cache for 10 minutes.

Cost/latency back-of-envelope (very rough):
- Avg (non-report) convo: retrieve 3 chunks (3*800 tokens->embeds), rerank 20 chunks, decode ~150 tokens -> expected 95th pct latency 350-600ms on A100 per request with batching disabled; with mild batching (50ms window) throughput increases.
- Embedding cost is mainly local compute — their Milvus + embedder throughput should be benchmarked (I'll ask infra to run embedder perf on their nodes).

Action items (owners + tentative dates):
- Maya: produce a one-page playbook for on-prem Private install checklist (network, KMS, control-plane windows) — due 2025-02-20.
- Ethan: escalate autoscaler feature gaps with infra team; capture constraints doc for on-prem (JIRA-PL-456) — due 2025-02-21.
- Sara (PLI): provide sample dataset (anonymized) and a small subset (100 docs) for initial indexing and perf tests — target 2025-02-18.
- Jin (PLI): confirm legal requirements and send NDA/SOC2 addendum request to Redwood legal — noted as blocker for formal private deployment.
- PLI + Redwood: schedule on-site bench week (if NDA OK) or remote perf run; tentative week of 2025-03-03.

Open questions (need answers before next call):
- Do they require model weights to be fully air-gapped (no control-plane verification)? If yes, need signed offline bundle process.
- What is their per-request SLAs for report windows? 1s tail vs 2s tail will change design.
- Any regulatory constraints on embeddings retention / ability to delete vector entries on request? (GDPR-ish).

Prompting notes / sample prompt patterns we recommended in the call:
- Retriever-first pattern: "Given the following documents (ids + snippets), answer concisely using only those excerpts. If not in provided text, say 'not in documents'." -> encourages grounded answers.
- Reranker prompt: short prompt to instruct model to score relevance 0-1; we then use scores to reorder. Keep reranker context <= 512 tokens.

Quick test plan (mini POC):
1) PLI to provide 100 anonymized docs + canonical questions (50 Qs).
2) Redwood spins up Private preview container on Redwood infra but with same network constraints (to simulate). Run embedder indexing + retrieval latency tests.
3) Validate end-to-end quality (F1 on QA where applicable) and tail latency.
4) If results ok, schedule remote on-prem perf run or on-site week.

Notes-to-self (things to write into playbook):
- Prep script to re-chunk and re-tokenize PLI documents; include a dry-run that outputs token histograms.
- Small utility: convert Milvus metadata -> Redwood required schema (doc_id, chunk_id, offset, text, meta.json).
- Check HSM/KMS compatibility matrix: PLI runs HashiCorp Vault; verify Redwood Private KMS integrations
- Fallback policy: if primary quantized model fails on a request, fallback to smaller fp16 variant (adds latency but keeps availability).

Random customer quotes (save for readback):
- Jin: "We can't have anything fragile during our 8pm reporting window — latency spikes are show-stoppers."
- Sara: "If embeddings drift, our search quality tanks. We need an easy re-index path we can run weekly."

Next call: 2025-02-24 (tentative) — agenda: review 100-doc POC results, legal status, autoscaler gaps.

End of notes.
